host_baseline.basis: measured once with the pinned host and a role's structured-output tool (athena.toml [agents]); not measured per invocation

input.basis: Claude Code result.modelUsage for the requested model

output.basis: Claude Code result.modelUsage for the requested model

cache_read.basis: Claude Code result.modelUsage for the requested model

cache_write.basis: Claude Code result.modelUsage for the requested model

cost.basis: Claude Code total_cost_usd, at list price

commands_run: cargo fmt --all && cargo test -p athena-core --lib -q design_check
cargo fmt --all && cargo test -p athena-core -q --test refusal_corpus
cargo fmt --all && cargo test -p athena-cli -q check_reading

policy_denials.detail: git status --short | head; wc -l crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs crates/athena-context/src/briefs/reader.rs crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs; sed -n 170,300p crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs

python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
p='crates/athena-context/src/briefs/reader.rs'
s=open(p).read()
start=s.index('pub const CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE')
end=s.index('/// The reader brief: the request')
new='''pub const CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE: &str = "Before you give behavior criteria for a code or tests change, read the code and write one assumption that starts \\
with `Code survey:` and names the crates/ paths you read, with these labels (`check_behavior_test_design`): `Entry point:` identifiers; \\
`Gate order:` identifiers in run order; `Stop gate:` one of them; `Reuses:` identifiers or no existing function; `Output:` no new output, \\
`AnyRecord::<Variant>` or a round-trip test deliverable; `Direct check: criterion N` for each behavior criterion, naming an entry point, a gate \\
or a model call, not a skip switch or an internal helper. A criterion that only says fmt, clippy and test pass needs none. \\
When the request adds or tightens a refusal rule, also write a criterion that says the change refuses more readings and the higher refusal rate is intended. \\
Say how many: write `expected N% of newly refused readings` (a whole percent). A replay of past readings holds the job when more than N plus 5 points \\
of them are newly refused, and when you give no number it holds the job above 10%. For N above 25, also write, in a criterion or in out_of_scope, \\
one sentence with `because`, `now asks` or `new required` that says why past readings should be refused; the verifier is shown it.";

/// A filled-in `Code survey:` assumption that `check_code_survey` and `check_behavior_test_design` in athena-core
/// accept. The refusal errors of both checks end with it. It is not part of the reader brief, which has no room
/// for it. It measures a property of its own survey: it is an example of the form, not text to paste under an
/// unrelated criterion.
pub const CODE_SURVEY_EXAMPLE: &str = "Code survey: crates/foo/src/run.rs. Entry point: `run_job`. \\
Gate order: `resolve`, `probe`, `report`. Stop gate: `probe`. \\
Reuses: `shared_helper`; no existing function checks gate order. Output: no new output. \\
Direct check: criterion 1 counts the calls `run_job` makes to `probe` and asserts the count is 1, not a skip switch or a read of an internal helper.";

'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE, CRITERIA_RULES_HEADING","CODE_SURVEY_EXAMPLE, CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE, CRITERIA_RULES_HEADING",1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
sed -n 24,36p crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs
echo $CARGO_TARGET_DIR && cargo test -p athena-context reader_brief 2>&1 | tail -30
cargo test -p athena-core --lib reading 2>&1 | grep -E "FAILED|failed|panicked|test result"
